hairline-tattoo.text: Users get scalp micropigmentation to create the look of a closely shaved head or added density along a thinning hairline, and to conceal transplant scars. The visible change is immediate; sourcing is mostly industry and press, with no clinical trials found.

sulfate-free-shampoo.text: Sulfate-free shampoo is chosen by people who want gentler cleansing for hair that looks soft and shiny, especially colored or dry hair. The benefit is a marketing premise; no trials have tested appearance outcomes.

co-washing.text: Users with dry, curly or textured hair co-wash to keep moisture in and cut frizz so curls look smoother and more defined. It is reported mainly through hair-care communities, and appearance outcomes are untested in trials.

olaplex-bond-builder.text: Olaplex is used by people with bleached or heat-styled hair who want it to look and feel less damaged. The repair mechanism is described by the company; evidence in the sources is company-cited testing rather than independent trials.

keratin-smoothing-treatment.text: A salon keratin treatment is used to straighten frizz and add shine, with results visible right away and lasting a few months. Users choose it for a sleeker head of hair; the smoothing is the cosmetic effect itself.

perm-texture-perm.text: Forum users get perms for added texture and volume, with posters claiming a boost of about 1 PSL and a way to cover weaker eye-area features. The curl change is visible at once; no attractiveness research backs the rating claims.

hair-relaxer-chemical-straightener.text: Relaxers are used to permanently straighten tight curls for a sleek, straight look, with new growth returning to natural texture. The straightening is visible straight away; cancer and fibroid links are under ongoing research.

hair-botox-hair-filler-treatment.text: Hair botox is a marketing name for smoothing treatments that are promoted to cut frizz and add shine. The look is cosmetic and visible after application; the term has no fixed formula and no direct trials.

deep-conditioner-hair-mask.text: People use a deep conditioner or hair mask on dry or damaged hair for softness and shine after a longer contact time. The improvement in feel and look is immediate but temporary, as these products coat the hair rather than repair it.

leave-in-conditioner.text: Leave-in conditioner is applied after washing for daily softness, detangling and frizz control. The smoothing effect is visible right away and temporary, and some formulas add heat protection.

chain: Cold water at end of wash
cold-water-rinse.text: Proponents finish washes with cold water in the belief that it closes the cuticle and adds shine. The idea is popular in hair-care circles; nobody has published a test of the shine effect.

apple-cider-vinegar-rinse.text: Users pour diluted apple cider vinegar over hair after washing, promoted as clarifying buildup and adding shine. The appearance claim rests on anecdote and has not been tested in trials.

rice-water-rinse.text: Users apply fermented rice water after shampooing, with claims that it strengthens hair, reduces breakage, adds shine and helps hair grow longer. It has a long traditional use; research is thin.

egg-hair-mask.text: An egg mask is used at home as a kitchen-ingredient protein treatment for dry, damaged or weak-feeling hair. It is popular in hair-care circles, and no trials have tested it.

chain: Thick oil on hair, brows, lashes
castor-oil.text: Users rub castor oil on scalp, brows and lashes in hopes of thicker, longer growth, and the oil also coats hair like a conditioner. It is established as a laxative; its growth effect on hair is untested.

chain: Traditional herbs as oils or pastes
ayurvedic-amla-bhringraj-shikakai.text: Amla, bhringraj and shikakai are Ayurvedic herbs used as powders, pastes or oils for cleansing and conditioning hair, and promoted for hair strength and growth. They have centuries of traditional use and no clinical hair trials.

satin-bonnet-durag.text: Durags and satin bonnets are worn to hold waves in place and protect hair overnight, so styles look neater the next day. They are a cultural staple of Black hair care; no clinical trials exist.

360-waves-wave-brush.text: Wave brushing, with a durag and pomade, trains short coily hair into a ripple pattern around the whole head. The pattern builds up over weeks of consistent brushing; it is a cultural staple with no clinical research.

hair-texture-powder-sea-salt-spray.text: Sea salt spray and texture powder are used to add volume, grip and a matte, tousled finish. The change is visible immediately after styling; some users also claim the spray makes hair wavier.

blow-dry-and-volumizing-routine.text: Looksmaxxing and grooming circles use blow-drying as a low-cost way to give hair more height and body, changing how full it looks. The lift is visible straight away and washes out.

heat-protectant.text: Heat protectants are used before blow dryers and irons to limit damage so hair keeps its shine and smoothness. They are marketed on this basis and untested in trials.

diffuser-curl-drying.text: Diffusers are used to dry curly, permed or fine hair with less frizz and more definition and volume. The look is visible after drying and temporary; no trials exist.

shower-filter.text: Shower filters are bought to reduce chlorine, which retailers link to dry skin and brittle hair. The skin and hair benefits are anecdotal.

scalp-exfoliation.text: Users exfoliate the scalp to clear flakes and product buildup, and some say it supports hair growth. There is some flaking data; no hair-growth trials exist.

protein-intake-for-hair.text: Hair and looksmaxxing communities suggest eating enough protein to support hair growth and quality, since hair is largely keratin. Deficiency links are noted; no trials test extra protein for hair.

chain: Building blocks for skin and hair
gelatin-bone-broth.text: Fans eat gelatin and bone broth in the belief that collagen supports skin and hair. The published record on appearance benefits is essentially empty.

brushing-technique-boar-bristle.text: Boar bristle brushes are used to smooth hair and are said to spread scalp oil along the strands for shine. The smoothing is a styling effect; the oil-distribution claim has no published tests.

haircut-for-face-shape.text: Styling and looksmaxxing advocates pick haircuts by face shape such as oval, round or square, to balance proportions. It is a popular rule of thumb with no published tests.

chain: Frames face with fringe or texture
middle-part-curtains-textured-crop-trend.text: Middle parts, curtains and textured crops are discussed as current men's cuts, with curtains linked to K-pop artists. The new look is visible once cut; no studies test effects on attractiveness.

gray-hair-reversal-supplements.text: People take copper, B12 and similar supplements hoping to restore natural hair color. Reversal is reported only where a deficiency caused the greying.
